newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE, CIS discuss tanker futures contract.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE, CIS discuss tanker futures contract.

text.p: Futures and options brokers CIS are discussing with the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) the possibility of launching a tanker freight futures contract, a company official said on Wednesday.

The official said the talks were proceeding "with a lot of caution" after attempts to launch a tanker futures contract known as TIFFEX failed in 1985 due largely to the lack of a credible index against which trades would be settled.
Industry sources said a tanker futures contract may be modelled on the dry bulk futures contract on BIFFEX, which was launched in 1985.
The Baltic Freight Index is set by a panel daily against a basket of 11 routes.
"We don't want to get it wrong," said the CIS official, who asked not to be named. ""We are consulting a lot of people in the industry...Talks are actively under way on a regular basis."
London-based CIS is a fully owned subsidiary of U.S. company Cargill Inc.
A LIFFE spokeswoman said BIFFEX "could act as a model" for the tanker contract.
But she added, "It is far too early to consider listing such a contract because there needs to be a transparent existing index."
The CIS official said points of discussion included what the index should comprise of, against what benchmark it should be set and which panellists should be used to set it.
No date had been set for the launch of the contract.
A tanker analyst said, "The idea has got more potential now (than in 1985) because the shipping industry has got a lot more sophisticated" about financial derivatives.
"An index has the intuitive appeal of simplicity. Once it has been established people can follow movements up and down very neatly even if you encompass more than one parameter.
"The index can be a composite of various factors, but you don't need to grapple with those factors separately," he added.
